record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Second variation and stability on Lie groups
record.original_question: For Lie groups and homogeneous spaces with known examples of minimal unit vector fields, determine the second variation of the volume functional at those fields and classify which examples are stable. In particular, go beyond the known computations for invariant minimal unit vector fields on three-dimensional Lie groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold and let $X:M\to T^1M$ be a smooth unit vector field, viewed as a section of the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ equipped with the Sasaki metric. The volume of $X$ is defined as
\[ \mathrm{Vol}(X) \;=\; \int_M \sqrt{\det\!\bigl(I + (\nabla X)^{*}\nabla X\bigr)}\, dv_g, \]
where $\nabla X$ is the covariant derivative of $X$. A unit vector field is called minimal if it is a critical point of $\mathrm{Vol}$ among unit vector fields (equivalently, its image is a minimal submanifold of $(T^1M,g_S)$). A minimal unit vector field is called stable if the second variation (Hessian) of $\mathrm{Vol}$ at $X$ is non-negative for every variation through unit vector fields.

Consider a Lie group $G$ (or, more generally, a homogeneous space) endowed with a left-invariant (resp. invariant) Riemannian metric, and let $X$ be a known minimal unit vector field on $G$ that need not be left-invariant nor restricted to dimension three.

Problem: 
(a) Compute the second variation (Hessian) of the volume functional $\mathrm{Vol}$ at such fields $X$, providing an explicit formula in terms of the Lie-algebraic and curvature data of $G$.
(b) Using this Hessian, classify which of the known examples of minimal unit vector fields on Lie groups and homogeneous spaces are stable and which are unstable, going beyond the case of left-invariant minimal unit vector fields on three-dimensional Lie groups.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: the second variation of the volume functional has been computed at general minimal unit vector fields (Gil-Medrano–Llinares-Fuster), and stability has been determined for Hopf vector fields on odd-dimensional spheres and Berger spheres, and for left-invariant totally geodesic unit vector fields on three-dimensional Lie groups. A general computation and stability classification beyond the three-dimensional left-invariant setting on Lie groups and homogeneous spaces does not appear to be available, so the problem remains partially solved/open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Second variation of volume and energy of vector fields. Stability of Hopf vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the Hessian of the volume of unit vector fields at a minimal one and establishes stability of Hopf vector fields on S^3.
status_evidence.claim: General second-variation formula and stability for Hopf fields are known.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Left-Invariant Totally Geodesic Unit Vector Fields on Three-Dimensional Lie Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies stability/instability of left-invariant unit vector fields with totally geodesic image on three-dimensional Lie groups.
status_evidence.claim: Stability is known for 3D Lie groups in the left-invariant case.

status_evidence.title: Volume minimising unit vector fields on three dimensional space forms of positive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses minimizers of the volume functional on three-dimensional positively curved space forms.
status_evidence.claim: Progress restricted to three-dimensional settings; higher-dimensional Lie-group cases not classified.
